newsitem.title: USA: Orange Cty D.A. seeks rehearing in supervisor case.
newsitem.headline: Orange Cty D.A. seeks rehearing in supervisor case.

text.p: Orange County California's District Attorney on Wednesday asked a state appeals court to reconsider its decision to dismiss charges against two county supervisors accused of misconduct in connection with the county's bankruptcy.
The county District Attorney filed a petition for rehearing with the 4th District Court of Appeal, arguing that the court had misconstrued its position on certain matters.

In November, a 4th District Court of Appeal panel dismissed charges against Board of Supervisors chairman Roger Stanton and supervisor William Steiner, who faced removal from office had the accusations been sustained by a jury.
A county grand jury had accused Stanton and Steiner last December of failing to oversee former county Treasurer Robert Citron and other county finance officials.
They were also accused of voting to issue county debt without making adequate inquiries into the need for the borrowings and whether the county could repay them.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on December 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June.
A judge recently ordered Citron to spend a year in county jail and pay a $100,000 fine for his role in the county's bankruptcy, the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.
